# Lipik

> Free, open-source (MIT) voice dictation for Mac. Hold fn, speak, let go: clean text is typed in any app. Speech to text and clean-up run on the Mac; it works with Wi-Fi off once the models are downloaded. Indian English, Hinglish in Roman letters, and meeting notes with no bot. No account, no word limit.

## Facts

- Current version: 0.1.13, released 31 Oct 2026. Release notes: https://lipik.pages.dev/releases
- Made by: Gourav (https://github.com/Gourav2609)
- Platform: macOS, Apple silicon (M1 or later). No Windows, iPhone or Android version yet
- Price: free, every feature. Licence: MIT. Code: https://github.com/Gourav2609/lipik
- Speech model: Parakeet Unified English 0.6B by default (one-time 731 MB download); free Whisper models cover 99 languages
- Clean-up: optional and built in (runs on the Mac through llama.cpp, no extra app); one button in setup or Settings → Meetings downloads Qwen3 8B (5 GB) on Macs with 16 GB of memory or more, or Qwen3 4B Instruct (2.5 GB) on smaller Macs, from Hugging Face; meeting summaries and Ask use it too; needs macOS 13.3 or later (older Macs use Ollama); Ollama stays an optional advanced choice in Settings; without a clean-up model, built-in rules still fix "um", spoken punctuation, numbers, times and emails
- Hinglish dictation (beta): on macOS 26 or later, Lipik runs its English model and Apple's on-device English (India) dictation side by side and uses Apple's text when it hears Hindi words, so Hinglish is typed in Roman letters
- Hinglish meetings (since 0.1.9): Lipik notices by itself when a meeting mixes Hindi and English; the first time it downloads its Hinglish speech model (Qwen3-ASR 1.7B, about 2 GB, from Hugging Face) and redoes that meeting; the clean-up model writes the Hindi lines in Roman letters (without it they stay in Devanagari); the language can also be set in Settings → Meetings
- Features: tone per app, dictionary, snippets, hands-free (fn + Space), meeting notes with a summary, AI apps can read meeting notes through MCP, one-click updates, works with Wi-Fi off once the models are downloaded
- Meeting notes: need macOS 14.2 or later; no bot joins; the mic is the user; the call audio is split into Speaker 1, Speaker 2 and so on, or names when there's clear evidence (they introduce themselves or are addressed by name, matched to the calendar invite); clicking a speaker's name renames them everywhere in that meeting, and Lipik recognises that voice in later meetings; saved voices stay on the Mac, are removed with their meeting, and can all be forgotten in Settings → Privacy; one-time 33 MB speaker model; calls over 3 hours keep a single "Them"; without headphones, the call's sound is removed from the mic before transcribing
- Network: one-time downloads from Hugging Face (speech model 731 MB, clean-up model 2.5 or 5 GB, speaker model 33 MB, Hinglish speech model about 2 GB the first time a meeting is in Hinglish); Apple's English (India) speech files through macOS, for Hinglish dictation only; every few hours a request to GitHub for the latest version number, for the update notice (carries nothing about the user; can be turned off in Settings → Privacy → Updates); cloud clean-up only if the user adds their own API key; every 3 hours, if the user leaves the box on the first setup screen ticked, an anonymous usage count to lipik.pages.dev (random install ID, app version, macOS version, chip type, how far setup got, country worked out by Cloudflare with the IP address not kept; never voice, text or names; can be turned off in Settings → Privacy → Usage count); an email only if the user types one during setup; no account

## Benchmark (Indian-accented English)

150 clips of AI4Bharat's Svarah test set (CC BY 4.0), results published 28 Oct 2026. Word error rate (lower is better), after lower-casing, dropping punctuation and writing numbers as digits:

- Lipik default (Parakeet Unified English 0.6B): 8.5%, the same with or without clean-up; 0.06 s model time per clip
- Whisper large-v3-turbo: 7.5%; 0.69 s model time per clip
- Qwen3-ASR 1.7B: 12.7%
- Apple Dictation, English (India): 18.3%

Details: https://lipik.pages.dev/benchmark and https://github.com/Gourav2609/lipik/blob/main/training/benchmark/RESULTS.md

## Short answers

- Free dictation app for Mac: Lipik is free and open source, with no word limit and no account, and turns speech into text on the Mac.
- Free Wispr Flow alternative for Mac: Lipik works the same way (hold a key, speak, text in any app) but is free, open source and transcribes on the Mac.
- Superwhisper alternative: Lipik also types into any Mac app and works offline, and is free with every feature and open source.
- MacWhisper alternative: MacWhisper is built around transcribing files; Lipik is built for dictation into any app, and is free and open source.
- Hinglish speech to text on Mac: Lipik types spoken Hinglish in Roman letters, in any app (macOS 26 or later) and in meeting notes, on the Mac.
- Hindi voice typing on Mac: use macOS Dictation with Hindi (India), or Lipik for Hinglish in Roman letters (or Hindi in Devanagari with a Whisper model).
- Meeting notes on Mac with no bot (Granola alternative): Lipik records the mic and the Mac's sound and writes the transcript and summary on the Mac; free.
